learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the physics of getting things done! Learn how force creates work, how energy shifts forms, and how simple machines make our lives easier.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In science, 'Work' is only done when a force causes an object to MOVE in the direction of the force ($W = F \times d$). Pushing a heavy wall without moving it might make you tired, but scientifically, you did ZERO work!
Energy is the ability to do work. It comes in many forms: Kinetic (movement), Potential (stored due to position/height), Thermal (heat), Chemical (food/batteries), and Electrical.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. For example, a falling ball turns its Potential energy (height) into Kinetic energy (speed).
Power is how FAST work is done ($P = W / t$). Two machines might do the exact same amount of work, but the one that does it faster has more Power. The unit of power is the Watt (W).

Simple machines (like levers, pulleys, and inclined planes) do not change the total AMOUNT of work. Instead, they change the amount of force needed by changing the distance over which the force is applied.

fun_activity.title: 🛹 The Ramp Race
fun_activity.instructions: Try lifting a heavy box straight up onto a table. Then, use a long wooden board as a ramp (inclined plane) and push the box up. Pushing it up the ramp feels much easier, right? You applied less force, but over a longer distance. The total work done is exactly the same!

exam_tips: 📌 Remember that if displacement is zero (object didn't move) or if force and displacement are perpendicular (like carrying a bag on your head while walking forward), Work Done is ZERO.
📌 Know the formulas: Kinetic Energy ($KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$) and Potential Energy ($PE = mgh$).
📌 1 kilowatt (kW) = 1000 Watts. Electrical energy is often measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh), which is the commercial unit (1 unit on your electricity bill).
quick_recap: ⭐ The standard unit for both Work and Energy is the Joule (J).
⭐ A pendulum beautifully demonstrates the constant back-and-forth conversion between kinetic and potential energy.
⭐ Power tells us the rate of energy consumption.
